annotations.title: Optimise a cut list: stock lengths and sheet layouts

description: Optimises a cut list: pieces of given lengths cut from the stock lengths a merchant sells (timber, studs, joists, rafters, rebar, trim), or rectangles nested on sheets (plasterboard, drywall, plywood, OSB, tiles) in straight edge-to-edge cuts. Gives the stock or sheets to buy, a cutting plan per bar or sheet, the real waste and a lower bound. Quantities only: no prices, no structural design.

detail.description: full (the default): the whole answer. summary: the result lines, the citation line and the page only — fewer tokens to read.

inputUnits.description: Send "base" to pass bare numbers on dimensioned inputs in base units (m, m², L, kg …), as the published test vectors are written. Without it a length, area or volume must carry its unit.

kerf.description: The saw's kerf, charged on every piece (both ways on a sheet). Left out, the material's: 3 mm or 1/8 in for a saw, none for a bar shear or a board knife.

kind.description: linear: lengths cut from stock lengths (studs, plates, joists, rafters, bars, trim, boards). sheet: rectangles nested on sheets (plasterboard or drywall, plywood, OSB, tiles).

material.description: What is cut, for the market's stock lengths or sheet sizes, saw kerf and grain when they are left out: timber (the default for linear), rebar or casing; plasterboard (the default for sheet), plywood, OSB or tile.

minOffcut.description: linear: the shortest offcut worth keeping; shorter ones count as waste.

pieces.description: The cut list: up to 200 lines and 3000 pieces (1500 for sheets) in all.

height.description: sheet: the piece's height (along the grain), with its unit.

join.description: linear: a run that may be joined where a stock length runs out (a plate, a rim, trim, a board run). Left out, a piece longer than every stock length is listed, not split: a joint in a joist, a rafter or a bar is the designer's.

length.description: linear: the finished length, with its unit.

rotate.description: sheet: whether this piece may turn a quarter; left out, as the request says.

width.description: sheet: the piece's width, with its unit.

rotate.description: sheet: whether pieces may turn a quarter (no grain or strength axis to keep). Left out: yes for plasterboard and tiles, no for plywood and OSB.

sheets.description: sheet: the sheet sizes on offer (the plan takes the one that buys the least area). Left out, the market's usual size for the material.

stock.description: linear: the stock lengths on offer, each in any number, with units ("4.8 m", "16 ft"). Left out, the market's usual lengths for the material in the system asked for.

system.description: The unit system inputs left out open in, and the one the page link opens in. The answer comes in both.

name: optimise_cuts

text.description: In the system asked for, then the other.

bound.description: The floor no plan can beat: the pieces with their kerf over the stock (with one stock length, at least one bar for each piece over half a bar; on sheets, one sheet for each piece too big to share one).

buy.description: What to buy: each stock length or the sheet size, and how many.

text.description: In the system asked for, then the other.

gapPercent.description: How far this plan is above the bound, percent.

given.description: What the plan was worked from, in both systems: the stock lengths or sheet sizes, the kerf, the minimum offcut, whether pieces turn.

patterns.description: Each way a bar or sheet is cut, with how many are cut that way; up to 150, most used first.
